clue.text: Substitute judge accepts story

indicators.note: the judge accepts, i.e. takes in, the story, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: REF is short for referee, a sports judge
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A stand-in judge is willing to believe someone's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a replacement worker who takes over a shift from another.

clue.text: I can read somehow in bright light

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of I can read are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone finds they can make out the text when the light is strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of I CAN READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is a glowing brilliance, the quality of shining brightly.

clue.text: It is held to provide a clearer view of things

definitions.text: It is held to provide a clearer view of things

parts.words: It is held to provide a clearer view of things
parts.note: describes a pair of spectacles on a handle, held up to the eyes rather than worn

explanation.surface: An argument or opinion is maintained because it clarifies matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is held' suggests an opinion held; literally the item is held in the hand, being eyeglasses on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeglasses mounted on a long handle are lifted by hand to see more sharply.

clue.text: Teachers surround a head

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word Teachers surround the letters wanted, which sit within it

explanation.surface: Staff gather around their headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a headteacher, but 'a head' means per person.
explanation.definitionFit: Priced at so much a head means per person, the same as every one individually.

clue.text: Cocktail drunk before the dance

indicators.note: before places the word for drunk ahead of the dance in the answer

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone gets tipsy ahead of the evening's ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A highball is a mixed drink of spirit and soda served in a tall glass.

clue.text: Urchin learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is traditional knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A street child is being taught how to ask for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead or entreat earnestly.

clue.text: Audience standing up, well-pleased with one's address

parts.note: the house is a theatre's audience
proud can mean projecting or standing up above a surface

explanation.surface: Theatregoers rise in an ovation, delighted with a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a speech, but it means one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone house-proud takes great pleasure in keeping their home immaculate.

clue.text: Big vessel in sea or tank

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words sea or tank

explanation.surface: A large ship is found either on the ocean or in a water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, the largest blood vessel.

clue.text: These clues may be ancient

parts.note: plays on crossword answer slots and on the legal phrase ancient ... for a long-standing right to daylight through windows

explanation.surface: A remark that the puzzles are very old.
explanation.walkthrough: In crossword jargon the entries in the grid are called by this word, and English property law protects ancient ones, meaning windows with a long-established right to daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Grid entries are traditionally termed so by setters, and windows letting in daylight share the name.

clue.text: Occasion when spirits are called for

definitions.text: Occasion when spirits are called for

parts.words: Occasion when spirits are called for
parts.note: reads like ordering drinks at a bar but describes summoning ghosts

explanation.surface: A time when someone orders whisky or gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests alcohol; here they are ghosts called up by a medium.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sitting with a medium, participants try to contact the dead.

clue.text: Most inexpensive hat priced wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly signals that the letters of hat priced are set out in a wrong, different order

explanation.surface: A hat has been given an incorrect, very low price tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges HAT PRICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going for next to nothing is about as cheap as can be.

clue.text: Dismantle ruin collapsing with gravity

indicators.note: collapsing means the word ruin falls apart and its letters re-form

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity or gravitational acceleration

explanation.surface: Taking apart a crumbling ruin under the pull of gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges RUIN to give UNRI.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a ship of its ropes and tackle is to take its rigging down.

clue.text: Bill born with spots on the face

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
né means born, used of a man's original name

explanation.surface: A man named Bill was born with a spotty face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin condition produces pimples, especially in teenagers.

clue.text: I learnt to become racialist

indicators.note: become says the letters of I learnt to turn into something else

parts.note: the printed words are the fodder, read with a second N as the setter intended, per the setter's slip

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they were taught to be a racist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' rearranges the fodder, but I LEARNT TO is one N short of the ten letters needed: a slip in the clue as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A racialist is bigoted, refusing to accept people of other races.

clue.text: Figure part out of shape? Try eating this

indicators.note: out of shape says the letters of figure part are bent into a new form

explanation.surface: A dieter whose body is out of shape is advised to eat a breakfast fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of shape' rearranges FIGURE PART.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus is a classic slimming breakfast, so a dieter might be told to try it.

clue.text: Set resting place next to lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Someone sets a bed down beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-knit exclusive circle of people is a clique.

clue.text: Make a mistake and run for it

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone blunders and then flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run for it' looks like fleeing; 'for it' links to the definition 'run', a short trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A short journey to do a task, such as going to the shops, is a run.

clue.text: The Pony Express's first and last new recruits

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
first and last picks the opening and closing letters of Express

explanation.surface: Riders newly signed up for the Pony Express mail service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last' takes E and S from Express; 'new' rearranges them with THE PONY. The Pony Express was a US horseback mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophytes are beginners or novices newly joining a group.

clue.text: Croesus, upset about banking initially, doesn't make it clear

indicators.note: about means the rearranged name goes around another letter
upset means the name Croesus is knocked over and rearranged
initially takes the first letter of the word banking

explanation.surface: Croesus, the rich king, is annoyed about banking and is evasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges CROESUS to OSCURES and 'about' puts B (first of banking) inside. Croesus was a legendary wealthy king.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to make it hard to see or understand.

clue.text: He has absolute control of the French vessel

parts.note: des is French for of the, plural
a pot is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A French ship whose captain wields complete command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant ruling with unlimited power is an autocrat.

clue.text: Travelling goods will be in it

definitions.text: Travelling goods will be in it

parts.words: Travelling goods will be in it
parts.note: goods on the move are said to be in this state while being conveyed

explanation.surface: A remark about where merchandise sits during shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight being carried from place to place is described with this word for passage.

clue.text: Restored clubroom lacks right amount of electricity

indicators.note: restored suggests the remaining letters are rebuilt in a new order
lacks means one letter is missing from the word clubroom

explanation.surface: A clubroom that has been refurbished is missing the right amount of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes R from CLUBROOM, leaving CLUBOOM; 'Restored' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electric charge is named after the physicist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb.

clue.text: He received his rents mid-month

parts.note: reads like a landlord paid on the fifteenth, but rents means tears or stab wounds, received on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: A landlord collects payments in the middle of each month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rents' looks like payments; it means rips, the dagger wounds suffered on the Ides (the 15th) of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman dictator was stabbed to death on the Ides of March, 44 BC.

clue.text: Remains in rows

explanation.surface: Leftovers lying in lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover fragments of food are bits; fights or quarrels are also squabbles by this name.

clue.text: Out of clean forks? Use spoon for this breakfast food

indicators.note: out of indicates the letters of clean forks are put out of order

explanation.surface: No clean forks left, so eat cereal with a spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' looks like 'having none'; it rearranges CLEAN FORKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasted maize flakes are a popular cereal eaten with milk.

clue.text: Check the key in, that's the rule

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Checking the key is inserted is the regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places G inside REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of rule is a sovereign's time on the throne.

clue.text: Smart bird with no tail

indicators.note: with no tail means the last letter of the word for a bird is cut off

parts.note: a chick is a young bird

explanation.surface: An elegant bird lacking its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tail' removes the final K from CHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and fashionable people are elegant.

clue.text: Iago upset by cost of changing money

indicators.note: upset means the letters of Iago are overturned into another order

explanation.surface: Iago is annoyed by currency exchange fees.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago is the villain of Shakespeare's Othello; 'upset' rearranges his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The premium or fee charged when exchanging one currency for another.

clue.text: Valediction announcement that is given to university

parts.note: an ad is an announcement or advertisement

explanation.surface: A farewell speech announced to the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a farewell, a goodbye.

clue.text: Start to shake with mirth that's killing

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of the word shake

parts.note: laughter is mirth

explanation.surface: Someone begins shaking with laughter at something hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing' suggests hilarious; it means massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is the brutal killing of many people or animals.

clue.text: Holiness surprisingly intact in the outskirts of Surrey

indicators.note: in says the rearranged word sits inside the other letters
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of Surrey
surprisingly signals the letters of intact come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Holiness has unexpectedly survived on the edge of a commuter county.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county; 'the outskirts of' takes its edges, and the rearranged fodder sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is sacredness, the quality of being holy.

clue.text: Elevates one among many

indicators.note: among puts the letter for one inside the word for many

parts.note: hosts are great numbers, multitudes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Raising one person above the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' places I inside HOSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise or lift up, often with ropes.
